section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a single present study that aimed to replicate prior findings regarding connectedness to nature and body appreciation using the BAS-2 in community adults in the U.S., and to examine direct and indirect (via self-esteem) associations between nature exposure, connectedness to nature, and body appreciation. The study also planned to assess broader body-image variables (appearance investment, perceived sociocultural pressure, and internalisation) and to evaluate models separately for women and men using path analysis.
section_summary.evidence_source: The present study had a number of inter-related aims... We did so using a more conceptually valid measure of body appreciation (i.e., the BAS-2 ... ) and in a new, but culturally-similar, population (i.e., community adults in the U.S...). ... In addition, because of the possibility of sex-specific effects (Swami, Ng, et al., 2016), model fit was assessed separately for women and men. To test these different hypotheses, we used path analysis to develop a conceptual integration of the possible predictors of body appreciation.
